title: Workarounds in calling code for koffi's own behaviour: a zeroed record because a null pointer crashes, the runner editing its own environment because an explicit block fails, a real process handle because the pseudo-handle cannot be expressed, and the error code fetched by a second foreign call
Windows structure layouts declared by hand as strings, size-asserted at load and checked by a separately compiled C++ probe, with evidence for 64-bit Windows only

About 460 lines of C need a build matrix of operating system by processor by C library, four native CI runners, five npm packages and 13 pack, verify and release scripts; a platform outside the matrix has no launcher and no lock
The remote SSH helper ships the Landlock launcher as a separate file beside its single-file executable and needs a module-resolution hook to find it

reason: The workspace exists to compile two C programs per operating system, processor and C library and to publish them as npm packages; the Go design compiles the launch stage and the lock into the harness binary with go build, so the C sources, the platform packages, the build matrix and the release procedure are not carried, while the launcher and lock behaviour they tested is kept as requirements.

The Landlock launcher becomes a hidden launch stage of the dsh binary that builds its ruleset with go-landlock, enforces it on one locked thread and then replaces itself with the command, reporting status on a separate descriptor instead of exit code 125; the flock binding becomes a direct syscall.Flock call from the standard library.

The goal of the decision, that installing the harness never compiles anything, is kept and is met by Go itself; the mechanism, a family of prebuilt native packages with a Node-API addon and a static launcher, is not carried, because the binary makes the Landlock and flock system calls directly and the addon's asynchronous machinery exists only for JavaScript's single thread.

Every operating-system function upstream reaches through this foreign-function addon (write-through rename, kernel lock, permission-preserving replace, token and job process start, access-control edits, process table, process replacement) is called from Go through typed wrappers in golang.org/x/sys or the standard library, with a short list of functions bound by hand and no cgo.

It exists only to hand upstream's JavaScript the private module-loader modules of Node, for code hot reload, profile package resolution and manifest cache clearing; a Go binary has no run-time module loader, first-party code is linked in and plugins are separate processes, so there is nothing to reach.

The entry allows koffi's install script, which compiles from source when no prebuilt binary is present, and records an exact pin to 3.1.1 in nine manifests because the 3.3.2 source build fails under GCC 13; golang.org/x/sys is plain Go source compiled by the Go compiler for every target, so there is no install script, no source-build fallback and one go.mod line instead of nine pins.

The entry denies an npm install script that pnpm would otherwise refuse to skip silently; install scripts are an npm mechanism, downloading a Go module runs no code, and the package itself has no Go counterpart.

The exemption exists because the addon family must be re-released and installed at once for each Node and V8 build it has to recognise, here Electron 44.7.0; the Go design has no component that depends on private runtime interfaces, so nothing has to bypass a release-age rule when the runtime changes.

The exemption exists because this addon works only with Node and V8 builds whose fingerprint it recognises, so a fresh release had to be installed immediately for Electron 44.7.0; harness code in Go never reaches into runtime internals, so no component is tied to a runtime build.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt macOS arm64 binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform binary to exempt.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt macOS x64 binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform binary to exempt.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt Linux arm64 glibc binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform or per-C-library binary to exempt.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt Linux arm64 musl binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform or per-C-library binary to exempt.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt Linux x64 glibc binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform or per-C-library binary to exempt.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt Linux x64 musl binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform or per-C-library binary to exempt.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt Windows arm64 binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform binary to exempt.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt 32-bit Windows binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform binary to exempt.

This is the same release-age exemption repeated for the addon's prebuilt Windows x64 binary, because the policy matches exact package names; with no addon in the Go design there is no per-platform binary to exempt.

A Go wrapper takes typed arguments, accepts nil where Windows does and returns the error of the same call, and the standard library passes an explicit environment block to CreateProcessAsUser, so none of the four workarounds for the foreign-function layer is needed.

The structures come from golang.org/x/sys as compiled Go types maintained per architecture by the Go project, so there are no layout strings, no load-time size assertions and no separate header probe to keep in step.

There is no native artefact in the Go design: the launch stage and the lock are Go source compiled for every target by go build from one machine, so the build matrix, the platform packages and the pack and release scripts have nothing to build or publish.
The launch stage is part of the one dsh binary, which is also the remote SSH helper, so a remote host has the stage without a second file and without a resolution hook.

title: Operating-system calls without a foreign-function layer (replaces koffi)
verified: go list -m -json, go mod download -json, LICENSE and the windows and unix source in the module cache, 2026-11-18, Go 1.27.4

title: One package per operating-system capability; no generic call-by-name layer
Hand-bound system functions and cgo imports appear only in the one binding package
Windows publication is write-through, refuses an existing name and never copies across volumes
Cross-process lock: contention is immediate, a killed holder releases it, readers are not blocked
A child starts under a token with an explicit environment inside a kill-on-close job, and a failed start leaves nothing behind
Replacing a file on Windows keeps its access-control list and never widens who can read the new content
Each hand-bound function is called on real Windows: restricted token and Low label
A process identity of ID plus creation time rejects a reused ID
Pure-Go builds for Linux, macOS and Windows contain no file of another system
Sandbox launch stage and POSIX process lock as harness code (replaces the native/system launcher and flock addon)
Landlock ruleset construction
verified: go list -m -json, go mod download -json, LICENSE, go.mod and the landlock source in the module cache, 2026-11-18, Go 1.27.4; its dependency kernel.org/pub/linux/libs/security/libcap/psx v1.2.78 (BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0-only) compiles C only when cgo is on

title: Build the ruleset with go-landlock; enforce it on one locked thread; then replace the process
A fixed reference set, strict creation, and three explicit refusals
No native artefact family; the lock is a system call in the process
The stage lives in the dsh binary, is dispatched first, and has a start-up budget
Access kinds per Landlock interface version, the file-only trim, and full or partial
A failure at any stage step never reaches exec, and the call order keeps the thread-bound calls together
The stage imports only allowed modules and starts with broken configuration and an unwritable home
Pure-Go static Linux builds with no C compiler, no cgo import, no landlocktsync tag and no all-threads restrict call
Launch-stage start-up delay stays within its budget on the release binary
POSIX lock contract with real descriptors and child processes on Linux and macOS
No environment variable or working directory changes which binary confines
Landlock confines a command and its children on a current kernel
An older kernel is reported partial and still confines; child results are never read as launcher failure
Without Landlock the stage refuses and the command never runs
The stage behaves the same in both build modes and on a musl system
Access to runtime-internal module loaders (not needed: a Go binary has no run-time module loader)
Harness code never reaches into runtime internals
No go:linkname directive, assembly file or disabled linkname check in the harness module
